release_gates: A branch marked starter contains no feature implementation; branch existence is not acceptance or a ready upstream PR.
Provider follow-ups must rebase onto main containing OCI before upstream review. Shared contracts remain independent provider-neutral PRs.
Run final scope/content review and required CI on the exact tested commit; no OCI-name branches or imports in shared runtime.
Preserve current auth/default/template/persisted-ID/retry/reconciliation/rollback/return/redaction contracts across each feature.
Use focused unit/mocked and required cross-provider tests, then separately authorized bounded live acceptance with independent cleanup verification.
Close applicable image/container/API security, persistence and scheduler/workload checks before production/HA/all-shape/RDMA claims.

decisions: Keep the current direct-instance provider baseline and adopt capabilities selectively rather than replacing transport/configuration contracts.
The initial explicit-template-attribute suggestion is insufficient alone because conversion/output paths can drop or overwrite values; HF-SHARED must establish preservation before HF-OCI.
Hardware facts are implemented; Symphony CPU policy/type labels/RAM units are design/deployment choices. No HostFactory production claim is made.
SDK is optional: preflight, placement, networking, tags, boot performance, secondary volumes and pools can use current CLI transport.
OKE manifests may advance in parallel. Live acceptance needs the chosen image/transport/auth model; SDK workload identity depends on SDK and OKE deployment foundations.
Generic identity/pool contracts are separate from OCI consumers. Scale authority/draining is mandatory; add another shared branch only when the design demonstrates a need.
Existing NSGs, Compute Cluster placement, capacity-only preemptible fallback and auth modes are preserved rather than reimplemented as gaps.
25 examples across 23 shapes mean authoring coverage. A prior single-worker canary does not establish all-shape/RDMA/OKE/Symphony acceptance.
Existing Azure/package PRs and maintainer-owned release follow-ups remain external; this roadmap does not duplicate their fixes.
All owners are unassigned roles; no dates or accountable people are invented. Rough single-engineer estimates overlap, exclude external waits/live costs and must not be summed.
Optional P2/P3 capabilities and their production gates do not become prerequisites for merging the bounded direct-instance contribution.
